title: Command injection, argument injection and LDAP
summary: Process.Start through a shell turns a host name into a command line. Start programs without a shell, pass ArgumentList, stop option injection with --, and escape LDAP filters the RFC 4515 way.

steps.title: The request, and the command line it builds
body: ```csharp fragment
Process.Start("/bin/sh", $"-c \"ping -c 1 {host}\"");
```text
GET /api/tools/ping?host=10.0.0.5          ->  sh -c "ping -c 1 10.0.0.5"
GET /api/tools/ping?host=10.0.0.5; id      ->  sh -c "ping -c 1 10.0.0.5; id"
uid=1442(shopsvc) gid=1442(shopsvc)

A **shell** reads the whole string and gives meaning to `;` `&&` `|` `$( )` backticks, newlines, `>` and quotes. Anything that reaches a shell is code. From `id` it is a short way to `env` (the app's secrets), `curl` to the internal network, or a reverse shell.

It is not only `/bin/sh` written out. These all go through a shell: `cmd.exe /c ...`, `powershell -Command ...`, `ProcessStartInfo { UseShellExecute = true }` with a constructed file name, Python's `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True)`, Node's `child_process.exec`, and `system()` in almost every language.

steps.prompt: Does this start the program through a shell (dangerous with user input) or directly?

steps.title: No shell, ArgumentList, and --
body: ```csharp fragment
var psi = new ProcessStartInfo("ping")        // the program itself, found on PATH
ArgumentList = { "-c", "1", "--", host },  // each item is one argument, passed as it is
UseShellExecute = false,                    // the default in .NET Core and later
With no shell, `10.0.0.5; id` is one strange host name that `ping` cannot resolve. Three more things a reviewer checks:

1. **Argument injection.** No shell is needed to abuse a program's own options: a host of `-f` makes ping flood; a file name of `--output=/etc/cron.d/x` makes some tools write anywhere. `--` ends the options, so everything after it is a plain argument. Validate the shape too (an IP address, a host name).
2. **`Arguments` (one string) versus `ArgumentList`.** `Arguments = "-c 1 " + host` is split by .NET's own rules, so a space or a quote in `host` adds arguments. Use `ArgumentList`.
3. **A library instead of a process.** `System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping`, `System.IO.Compression.ZipFile`, an image library: no process, no command line, no injection.

steps.prompt: How many arguments does the program receive in each case?
code: foreach (var x in new[] { "-c", "1", "--", host }) b.ArgumentList.Add(x);
steps.explain: Both are 4, but not the same 4. The single string becomes `-c`, `1`, `10.0.0.5` and `-f`: the attacker added an option. The list passes `-c`, `1`, `--` and `10.0.0.5 -f` as one (invalid) host name.

steps.title: A ping command that cannot be injected
prompt: Write `ProcessStartInfo PingCommand(string host)` (`using System.Diagnostics;` and `using System.Net;` at the top). It returns a `ProcessStartInfo` for `ping` that the caller will start:

- `host` must be an IP address (`IPAddress.TryParse`) or a host name: labels of letters, digits and `-`, separated by dots, not starting or ending with `-`, at most 253 characters. Anything else throws `ArgumentException`, before a `ProcessStartInfo` exists.
solution: throw new ArgumentException("Not an IP address or host name.", nameof(host));
var psi = new ProcessStartInfo("ping") { UseShellExecute = false };
foreach (var a in new[] { "-c", "1", "-W", "1", "--", host }) psi.ArgumentList.Add(a);
hints: Validate first: `if (!IPAddress.TryParse(host, out _) && !Regex.IsMatch(host, @"...")) throw new ArgumentException(...);`. `$` in .NET also matches before a final newline: put the length check `(?=.{1,253}$)` in front, or use `\z`.
Build it with `new ProcessStartInfo("ping") { UseShellExecute = false }` and add each argument with `psi.ArgumentList.Add(...)`.
template: Dojo.Eq("FileName is ping, not a shell", "ping", ok.FileName);
Dojo.Eq("the arguments, one by one", new List<string> { "-c", "1", "-W", "1", "--", "10.0.0.5" }, ok.ArgumentList.ToList());
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("a trailing newline is refused", () => PingCommand("hub.example\nid"));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("an empty host is refused", () => PingCommand(""));

steps.title: LDAP filters inject too
body: Directory searches (Active Directory, OpenLDAP) use filters like `(&(uid=ada)(objectClass=person))`. Built by concatenation, a username of `*` matches everyone, and `ada)(|(uid=*` rewrites the filter:
```text
(&(uid=" + user + ")(userPassword=" + pw + "))
user = *)(uid=*))(|(uid=*      ->  (&(uid=*)(uid=*))(|(uid=*)(userPassword=...))

RFC 4515 defines the escaping for values in a filter: each of `\` `*` `(` `)` and the NUL character becomes a backslash and two hex digits: `\5c`, `\2a`, `\28`, `\29`, `\00`. `System.DirectoryServices.Protocols` has no helper for it, so teams write one, once, and use it for every value.

steps.title: Escape an LDAP filter value
prompt: Write `string LdapValue(string value)` that escapes a value for an LDAP search filter (RFC 4515): `\` → `\5c`, `*` → `\2a`, `(` → `\28`, `)` → `\29`, NUL (`\0`) → `\00`. Every other character stays as it is.
hints: Escape the backslash **first** if you use `Replace`, or (simpler) go character by character with a `switch` into a `StringBuilder`.
`'\\' => "\\5c"` in C# is: the character backslash becomes the text `\5c`.
template: Dojo.Eq("a plain name is unchanged", "ada.lovelace", LdapValue("ada.lovelace"));
Dojo.Eq("the filter-breaking payload is defused", "ada\\29\\28uid=\\2a", LdapValue("ada)(uid=*"));
Dojo.Eq("a backslash is escaped once, not twice", "a\\5cb\\2a", LdapValue("a\\b*"));
Dojo.Eq("accents stay as they are", "Zoë (sales)".Replace("(", "\\28").Replace(")", "\\29"), LdapValue("Zoë (sales)"));

steps.title: Live lab: run id on the shop, then remove the shell
prompt: In the **vulnerable shop** lab, do **Attack: run commands on the server** (read `DEPLOY_TOKEN` through the ping tool) and **Fix: no shell, validate, ArgumentList** in `Tools.cs`. The check tries `;`, `&&`, `|`, `$( )`, backticks, a newline and an option, and still pings `127.0.0.1`.
steps.explain: Without a shell nothing in the host string has a special meaning; validation and `--` stop the argument tricks a shell is not needed for.
